clauses.label: Sec. 2.
clauses.text:
Sec. 2. Financial Plans and Programs.  The Board of Governors 
of the Federal Reserve System, the Federal Home Loan Bank Board, 
the Farm Credit Administration, and the Board of Governors of the 
Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation, shall participate with the 
Office of Emergency Planning, the Department of the Treasury, and 
other agencies in the formulation of emergency financial and stabili­
zation policies. The Heads of such agencies shall, as appropriate, 
develop emergency plans, programs, and regulations, in consonance 
with national emergency financial and stabilization plans and policies, 
to cope with potential economic effects of mobilization or an attack, 
including, but not limited to, the following:

clauses.label: (a)
clauses.text:
(a) Money and credit.  Provision, restriction, or regulation of 
money and credit in accordance with the needs of the economy, includ­
ing the acquisition, decentralization, and distribution of emergency 
supplies of currency; the collection of cash items and non-cash items; 
and the conduct of fiscal agency and foreign operations.

clauses.label: (b)
clauses.text:
(b) Financial institutions.  Provision for the continued or resinned 
operation of banking, savings and loan, and other financial institu­
tions, including measures for the re-creation of evidence of assets or 
liabilities destroyed or inaccessible.

clauses.label: (c)
clauses.text:
(c) Liquidity.  Provision of necessary liquidity to financial institu­
tions including those destroyed or damaged.

clauses.label: (d)
clauses.text:
(d) Cash withdrawals and credit transfers.  Regulation of the dis­
tribution and withdrawal of currency and the transfer of credits in­
cluding deposit and share account balances.

clauses.label: (e)
clauses.text:
(e) Insurance. Provision for the assumption and discharge of 
liability pertaining to insured deposits and insured savings accounts 
or withdrawable shares in financial institutions destroyed or made
*  '" i insolvent.

clauses.label: Sec. 3.
clauses.text:
Sec. 3. Sharing o f War Losses. Heads of agencies shall, as appro­
priate, participate with the Office of Emergency Planning and the 
Department of the Treasury in the development of policies, plans, 
and procedures for sharing war losses.
S ec. 4. Securities and Exchange Commission.  In addition to its 
concern with other programs outlined herein, the Commission shall 
collaborate with the Secretary of the Treasury in the development of 
emergency financial control plans, programs, procedures, and regula­
tions for:

=== PDF page 28 of 149 ===
1856 THE PRESIDENT

clauses.label: (a)
clauses.text:
(a) Stock trading . Temporary closure of security exchanges, sus­
pension of redemption rights and freezing of stock and bond prices, if 
required in the interest of maintaining economic controls.

clauses.label: (b)
clauses.text:
(b) Modified trading.  Development of plans designed to re­
establish and maintain a stable and orderly market for securities when 
the situation permits under emergency conditions.

clauses.label: (c)
clauses.text:
(c) Protection o f securities. Provision of a national records system 
which will make it possible to establish current ownership of securities 
in the event major trading centers and depositories are destroyed.

clauses.label: (d)
clauses.text:
(d) Flow o f capital. The control of the formation and flow of 
private capital as it relates to new securities offerings or expansion of 
prior offerings for the purpose of establishing or re-establishing indus­
tries in relation to the~ nation’ s needs in or following a national 
emergency.

clauses.label: (e)
clauses.text:
(e) F light off capital. The prevention of the flight of capital out­
side this country and the impounding of securities in the hands of 
enemy aliens.
S ec. 5. Export-Im port B ark of Washington. Under foreign policy 
guidance of the Secretary of State, the Export-Import Bank shall 
develop plans for the utilization of the resources of the Bank in expan­
sion of productive capacity abroad for essential materials, foreign 
barter arrangements, acquisition of emergency imports, or in any other 
manner designed to strengthen the relative position of the Nation and 
its allies, or to assist neutral nations, and, under guidance of the Secre­
tary of the Treasury, develop plans for the utilization of the Bank’ s 
resources in support of the domestic economy and survival of the 
nation.
S ec. 6. Sm all Business Adm inistration. The Administrator of the 
Small Business Administration shall:

clauses.label: (a)
clauses.text:
(a) Prime contract authority.  Develop plans to administer a pro­
gram for the acquisition of prime contracts by the Administration 
and, in turn, for negotiating or otherwise letting of subcontracts to 
capable small business concerns in an emergency.

clauses.label: (b)
clauses.text:
(b) Resource information.  Provide data on facilities inventories 
and potential production capacity of small business concerns to all 
interested agencies.

clauses.label: (c)
clauses.text:
(c) Procurement. Develop plans to determine jointly with Fed­
eral procurement agencies, as appropriate, which defense contracts are 
to go to small business concerns and to *  certify to the productive and 
financial ability of small concerns to perform specific contracts, as 
required.

clauses.label: (d)
clauses.text:
(d) Loans for plant modernization.  Develop plans for providing 
emergency assistance to essential individual industrial establishments 
through direct loans or participation loans for the financing of pro­
duction facilities and equipment.

clauses.label: (e)
clauses.text:
(e) Resource pools. Develop plans for encouraging and approving 
small business defense production and research and development pools.

clauses.label: (f)
clauses.text:
(f) Financial assistance. Develop plans to make loans, directly or 
in participation with private lending institutions, to small business 
concerns and to groups or pools of such concerns, to small business 
investment companies, and to state and local development companies 
to provide them with funds for lending to small business concerns, for 
defense and essential civilian purposes.
S ec. 7. The Veterans Administration.  The Administrator of Vet­
erans Affairs shall;

clauses.label: (a)
clauses.text:
(a) Health functions.  Assist the Department of Health, Educa­
tion, and Welfare in the fulfillment of that Department’ s responsibili­
ties and participate with it in the development of plans and guidance 
to utilize to the maximum extent the existing health resources of the 
Veterans Administration.

=== PDF page 29 of 149 ===
FEDERAL REGISTER 1857Thursday, February 28, 1963

clauses.label: (b)
clauses.text:
(b) Veterans benefits. (1) Develop plans for the continuation or 
restoration of benefits to veterans of previous wars as soon as possible 
after a direct attack upon the United States and prepare operating 
plans and programs designed to recognize and care for new veterans.

(2) Develop emergency measures for the conduct of compensation, 
pension, rehabilitation, and insurance payments consistent with over­
all Federal plans for the continuation of Federal benefit payments 
after an enemy attack.

(3) Develop plans and procedures for the emergency conduct of 
insurance and loan guaranty functions in accordance with indirect 
stabilization policies and controls designed to deal with various condi­
tions of attack.
S ec. 8. Research. Within the framework of Federal research 
objectives, Heads of agencies shall supervise, conduct, or recommend 
research directly concerned with carrying out emergency preparedness 
responsibilities, designate representatives for necessary ad hoc or task 
force groups, and provide advice and assistance to other agencies in 
planning for research in areas involving their agency’ s interest.
S ec. 9. Cooperation w ith Department of Defense.  In consonance 
with national civil defense plans, programs, and operations of the 
Department of Defense under Executive Order No. 10952, Heads of 
agencies shall, as appropriate :

clauses.label: (a)
clauses.text:
(a) Facilities protection.  Provide facilities protection guidance 
material adapted to the needs of the facilities and services concerned 
and promote a national program to stimulate disaster preparedness 
and control in order to minimize the effects of overt or covert attack 
on facilities under their jurisdiction or influence. Guidance shall 
include, but not be limited to, organization and training of facility 
employees, personnel shelter, evacuation records protection, continuity 
of management, emergency repair, déconcentration or dispersal of 
facilities, and mutual aid associations for an emergency.

clauses.label: (b)
clauses.text:
(b) Damage assessment. Maintain a capability to assess the effects 
of attack on facilities under their jurisdiction and to provide data 
and assistance to the Department of Defense.
S ec. 10. Fv/nctional Guidance. Heads of agencies, in carrying out 
the functions assigned in this order, shall be guided by the following :

clauses.label: (a)
clauses.text:
(a) Interagency cooperation.  Heads of agencies shall enlist the 
cooperation of appropriate State authorities and shall coordinate 
the performance of their emergency preparedness functions with 
departments and agencies having primary or supporting functions 
related thereto.

clauses.label: (b)
clauses.text:
(b) Presidential coordination.  The Director of the Office of 
Emergency Planning shall advise and assist the President in determin­
ing policy for the performance of functions under this order and in 
coordinating the performance of such functions with the total national 
preparedness program.

clauses.label: (c)
clauses.text:
(c) Emergency planning.  Emergency plans and programs, and 
emergency organization structure required thereby, shall be developed 
as an integral part of the continuing activities of each agency on the 
basis that it will have the responsibility for carrying out such pro­
grams during an emergency. Heads of agencies shalf be prepared 
to implement all appropriate plans developed under this order. Modi­
fications and temporary organizational changes, based on emergency 
conditions, will be in accordance with policy determinations by the 
President.

clauses.label: Sec. 11.
clauses.text:
Sec. 11. Emergency Actions.  Nothing in this order shall be con­
strued as conferring authority under Title II I of the Federal Civil 
Defense Act of 1950, as amended, or otherwise, to put into effect 
any emergency plan, procedure, policy, program, or course of action 
prepared or developed pursuant to this order. Such authority is 
reserved to the President.

=== PDF page 30 of 149 ===
1858 THE PRESIDENT
S ec. 12. Resources Evaluation.  Heads of agencies shall provide 
for appropriate participation in the national resources evaluation 
program administered by the Office of Emergency Planning.
S ec. 13. Redelegation. Heads e f  agencies are hereby authorized 
■ to  redelegate within their agencies the functions hereinabove assigned 
to them.
S ec. 14. Prior Actions.  To the extent of any inconsistency be­
tween the provisions of any prior order and the provisions of this 
order, the latter shall control. Emergency Preparedness Order No. 
10 (heretofore issued by the Director of the Office of Civil and Defense 
Mobilization) (26 F.E. 835), and Defense Mobilization Orders No. 
1-20 dated January 15,1956 (21 F.E. 1127), No. 1-22 dated March 28, 
1956 (21 F.E. 2043), and 1-24 dated July 3, 1956 (21 F.E. 5057) 
(heretofore issued by the Director of the Office of Dexense Mobiliza­
tion) are hereby superseded and revoked.

versions.research_rationale: EO 11094 (signed 1963-02-26, 28 FR 1855-1858), read in full from the held official FR text: Sec. 1 Scope: the eight agencies (Heads of agencies); Sec. 2 Financial Plans and Programs (a)-(e); Sec. 3 Sharing of War Losses; Sec. 4 Securities and Exchange Commission (a)-(e); Sec. 5 Export-Import Bank of Washington; Sec. 6 Small Business Administration (a)-(f); Sec. 7 Veterans Administration (a)-(b); Sec. 8 Research; Sec. 9 Cooperation with the Department of Defense under EO 10952 (a)-(b); Sec. 10 Functional Guidance (a)-(c) (printed "Fv/nctional" in the text layer); Sec. 11 Emergency Actions (no authority to put plans into effect; reserved to the President); Sec. 12 Resources Evaluation; Sec. 13 Redelegation; Sec. 14 Prior Actions (this order controls over inconsistent prior orders; OCDM Emergency Preparedness Order No. 10 and Defense Mobilization Orders I-20, I-22 and I-24 superseded and revoked). It has no term or sunset. EO 11490 sec. 3015 item (21) revokes it, effective on signing 1969-10-28 (official text, PDF page 95; the APP transcription was not used). Inventory: the dossier's 28 clauses omit the Sec. 1 Scope and section lead-ins and mislabel or run paragraphs together; one override restates the inventory as 14 section clauses with no gap or overlap from Sec. 1 to the end of the last section. D6 / earlier-end and later-amendment test: the OFR catalog records only the EO 11490 revocation; the OLRC note at 42 U.S.C. 5195 note records only the EO 11490 revocation; the by-number scan of all 6,652 held FR order texts finds no order naming EO 11094: the only hits are pay-table figures (11,094.90) in EO 13715; the full EO 11490 text names it only in sec. 3015. The OFR note on EO 11490 prints the target date as 'February 26, 1993', an evident catalog typo for 1963. The signature date prints as 'February M, 1963' in the text layer; the FR Doc. 63-2219 filing line (Feb. 27, 1963) and EO 11490 item (21) fix it as February 26, 1963. No order amended, suspended, superseded or ended any clause between 1963-02-26 and 1969-10-28, so no later event is attached; the 1968 statutory renaming of the Office of Emergency Planning as the Office of Emergency Preparedness (Pub. L. 90-608; not held) changed the coordinating office's name, not the life of any clause. No report deadline, transcription or strike-and-reinsert question bears on the end. Savings: transferred_or_accrued (see savings_residuals).

savings_residuals.reason: Reading record LSP-EO_11490 (EO 11490, 34 FR 17567-17599, official FR text of FR-1969-10-30.pdf PDF pages 63-95 held by jobs/source-ladder, read in full; the American Presidency Project transcription was not used): sec. 101 says the order 'consolidates the assignment of emergency preparedness functions to various departments and agencies heretofore contained in the 21 Executive orders and 2 Defense Mobilization orders listed in Section 3015' and that 'Assignments have been adjusted to conform to changes in organization'; sec. 102(b) charges every department and agency with continuity-of-government planning; Parts 2-29 re-assign agency functions; Part 30 sets general provisions. Sec. 3014 ('Retention of Existing Authority') preserves existing assignments of functions 'Except as provided in Section 3015', so it expressly does not reach the revoked orders; sec. 3015 revokes 21 Executive orders and 2 Defense Mobilization orders without exception. There is no effective-date, pending-matter, transition or savings clause for any revoked order. Own-residual check, reading EO 11094 in full: it assigned to the Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, the Federal Home Loan Bank Board, the Farm Credit Administration, the Export-Import Bank of Washington, the FDIC Board of Directors, the Securities and Exchange Commission, the Small Business Administrator and the Administrator of Veterans Affairs national emergency preparedness planning functions, disclaimed any authority to put plans into effect, allowed redelegation and made the order control over inconsistent prior orders. EO 11490 Parts 16 (Export-Import Bank of the United States), 17 (Federal Bank Supervisory Agencies), 25 (Securities and Exchange Commission), 26 (Small Business Administration) and 29 (Veterans Administration) re-assigns the same agencies' emergency preparedness functions, adjusted to later changes in organization (sec. 101); that is a new assignment by the consolidating order, not a continuation of EO 11094. Plans and programs developed before 1969-10-28 are completed acts of the agencies and rest on their own statutes and on the new assignment; no held source shows any of them continued by force of this order. The revocation of OCDM Emergency Preparedness Order No. 10 and Defense Mobilization Orders I-20, I-22 and I-24 in its Prior Actions section was executed on issuance in 1963 and is not undone by revoking EO 11094. State transferred_or_accrued records the carry-forward of the assignment into EO 11490 and the completed acts; no clause of EO 11094 continues. Bounded search: the order and EO 11490 read in full in held official FR texts; a by-number scan of all 6,652 held official FR order texts (jobs/fr-originals, which hold every order number from 11091 to 11490; every hit read in context) and of the full EO 11490 text; the OFR catalog edges for the order (jobs/later-events EDGES.csv); the OLRC notes (jobs/current-law USC_EO_NOTES); the three machine searches (OFR catalog, U.S. Code, eCFR) read with their scope notes.
